# Comment-Like Constructs That Must Survive

Anything in this file is **not documentation**. It changes how a compiler,
linter, bundler, packager, or legal audit treats the code. Removing it is a
behaviour change, not a cleanup.

`scripts/preserve-patterns.txt` is the machine-readable version of this list and
is consumed by `scripts/audit-remaining.sh`. Add a pattern there whenever a new
construct is discovered, so the audit stops flagging it.

## Shebangs

`#!/usr/bin/env node`, `#!/bin/bash`, `#!/usr/bin/env python3`

Always the very first line. The kernel reads it. It is never the file's header
comment, even when it is the first `#` in the file — a header comment may follow
it on line 2 and should be kept separately.

## Directive prologues

`'use strict'`, `'use client'`, `'use server'`, `"use asm"`

These are string expression statements, not comments at all. Never in scope.

## Type-checker directives

| Ecosystem | Constructs |
|---|---|
| TypeScript | `// @ts-check`, `// @ts-nocheck`, `// @ts-ignore`, `// @ts-expect-error`, `/// <reference path=... />`, `/// <reference types=... />` |
| Flow | `// @flow` |
| Python | `# type: ignore`, `# type: <annotation>` (comment-form type hints — these are load-bearing), `# mypy: ...`, `# pyright: ...` |

Python comment-form type annotations (`x = []  # type: List[int]`) look like
trailing comments and are read by type checkers. Preserve them.

## Linter and formatter control

- ESLint: `eslint-disable`, `eslint-enable`, `eslint-disable-next-line`,
  `eslint-disable-line`, `eslint-env`, `global`/`globals`
- Biome / oxlint / dprint / Deno: `biome-ignore`, `oxlint-disable`,
  `dprint-ignore`, `deno-lint-ignore`, `deno-fmt-ignore`
- Prettier: `// prettier-ignore`
- Stylelint: `/* stylelint-disable */`, `/* stylelint-enable */`
- Python: `# noqa`, `# noqa: E501`, `# pylint: disable=...`, `# ruff: noqa`,
  `# fmt: off` / `# fmt: on` / `# fmt: skip` (Black)
- Go: `//nolint:...`, `//go:generate`, `//go:build`, `// +build`, `//go:embed`,
  `//go:linkname`, `//go:noinline`
- Security scanners: `# nosec`, `// NOSONAR`, `// CHECKSTYLE:OFF`
- Swift: `// swiftlint:disable`

`# fmt: off` / `# fmt: on` and `// prettier-ignore` come in pairs. Removing one
half silently reformats a block the next time a formatter runs.

## Coverage and bundler hints

`/* istanbul ignore next */`, `/* c8 ignore start */`, `/* v8 ignore next */`,
`/* webpackChunkName: "x" */`, `/* webpackPrefetch: true */`, `/* @vite-ignore */`,
`/*#__PURE__*/`, `/*#__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__*/`, `//# sourceMappingURL=...`,
`//# sourceURL=...`

`/*#__PURE__*/` sits inline in the middle of an expression. Removing it disables
tree-shaking and grows the bundle without any visible diff in behaviour.

## Legal notices

- SPDX: `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`, `SPDX-FileCopyrightText`
- Copyright lines, `All rights reserved`, `Licensed under ...`
- Full license headers (Apache, GPL, MPL, BSD blocks)
- `/*! ... */` — the bang marks a block that minifiers preserve deliberately
- JSDoc `@license` and `@preserve` tags

Treat a legal notice as preserved wherever it appears, not only at the top of
the file. A vendored snippet mid-file may carry its own attribution.

## Language pragmas

`#pragma once`, `#pragma pack`, `#pragma omp`, `#pragma GCC ...` (C/C++),
`pragma solidity ^0.8.0`, `pragma abicoder v2` (Solidity),
`# pragma: no cover` (Python coverage), `{-# LANGUAGE ... #-}` (Haskell),
`#![allow(...)]` and `#[derive(...)]` (Rust attributes — not comments at all).

## Generated-file markers

`// Code generated by ... DO NOT EDIT.`, `# @generated`

A file carrying one of these should not be edited at all. `find-candidates.sh`
already excludes files whose first five lines match; if such a marker shows up
mid-run, skip the whole file and say so in the report.

## Structural markers

`// #region` / `// #endregion`, `// MARK: -` (Swift/Xcode), `#region` (C#)

These drive editor folding and Xcode's jump bar. They are navigation, not prose.
Preserve by default; remove only on an explicit request.

## Framework-significant comments

- Vue: `<!-- @vue-ignore -->`, `<!-- eslint-disable -->` inside templates
- Angular: `<!-- i18n: ... -->` and `i18n` attributes
- Django/Jinja: `{# ... #}` is template syntax, and `{% comment %}` blocks may
  wrap markup that is intentionally disabled — never strip either implicitly
- Razor: `@* ... *@`
- Terraform/HCL: comments are ordinary, but `#` inside heredocs is not

## HTML and template comments

`<!-- ... -->` and EJS `<%# ... %>` are **out of scope by default**. They are
often used for markup structure, conditional comments, and CMS/ SSI directives
(`<!--#include -->`, `<!--[if IE]>`). Strip them only when the request names
them explicitly.
